chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Al-Minqari, from Fuzayl ibn Ayaz, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who is good during Islam, would he be seized for what he had done during the pre-Islamic period? So he (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who is good during Islam would not be seized for what he had done during the pre-Islamic period; but the one who is evil during Islam would be seized for the former and the latter.

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: the pre-Islamic period / Age of Ignorance
key_terms.يُحْسِنُ: to do good / to be good

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim's pre-Islamic sins get forgiven after conversion?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the scope of 'forgiveness of past sins' by distinguishing between general acceptance and specific accountability based on subsequent conduct. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that while Islam wipes the slate clean for the righteous, those who revert to pre-Islamic vices in their Islamic life are judged cumulatively, linking their past and present deeds. This principle underscores the dynamic nature of faith, where one's current trajectory determines the final valuation of their entire spiritual history.
